issues.legal_issue: Agricultural land belonging to an agriculturist cannot be attached before judgment or sold in execution of a decree for a debt unless the land was specifically mortgaged for that debt.
material_facts: The decree was obtained on a promissory note, not on the basis of a mortgage of the land.
The properties belonged to an agriculturist family and were sold in execution after an attachment made before judgment.
issues.conclusion: The attachment before judgment was invalid, and the execution sale made in pursuance of it was void.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14(1) of the Mysore Agriculturists’ Relief Act, 1928, agricultural land belonging to an agriculturist could not be attached or sold in execution of a decree unless specifically mortgaged for the debt to which the decree related. Section 14(2) permitted attachment only in execution of a decree; Section 14(3), which applied the procedure for attachment before judgment under Order XXXVIII of the Code of Civil Procedure, did not authorize a pre-judgment attachment of the land.

predicates.execution_sale_of_protected_agricultural: A creditor sought to sell agricultural land belonging to an agriculturist in execution of a decree.
predicates.land_not_mortgaged_for_the_debt: The land had not been specifically mortgaged to secure the debt underlying the decree.
predicates.attachment_made_before_judgment: The creditor attached the land before the court entered judgment on the debt.

issues.definition: When a creditor seeks an execution sale of protected agricultural land that was not mortgaged for the debt, an attachment made before judgment makes the attachment and resulting sale void.

issues.legal_issue: A person who becomes a member of a joint family after a void execution sale may sue to challenge that sale when the family retained ownership of the property.
material_facts: The properties belonged to a joint family, and the sale in execution conferred no title on the purchasers because it was void.
The plaintiffs were born after the sale and later brought a suit challenging its validity.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs acquired rights in the property by birth and were entitled to sue to question the sale.
issues.legal_principle: A void execution sale confers no title on the auction purchaser, so the joint family remains the owner of the property. A later-born member of that family acquires a right to the property by birth and may sue to challenge the sale.

predicates.suit_to_challenge_void_execution_sale: A claimant brought a suit seeking to invalidate an execution sale that was void.
predicates.property_owned_by_joint_family: The property belonged to a joint family that retained ownership because the sale transferred no title.
predicates.claimant_born_after_sale: The claimant was born after the execution sale.

issues.definition: A person born into a joint family after a void execution sale may challenge it when the family retained ownership of the property.

issues.legal_issue: A suit challenging an execution sale is not barred by res judicata when the claimants were neither parties to nor represented in the earlier suits, or when those suits were not decided by a court of competent jurisdiction.
material_facts: The claimants were not parties to the earlier suits, and they were not representatives of their father for the purposes of Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
The earlier suits were decided by a court that was not competent in relation to the court in which the present suit was filed.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not barred by res judicata.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires, among other things, that the matter have been heard and finally decided by a competent court and that the relevant parties or their representatives be bound by that decision. The claimants were not parties or representatives in the earlier suits, and those suits were not decided by a court of competent jurisdiction.

rule.if: suit_to_challenge_prior_execution_sale and ((not claimant_was_party_to_prior_suits and not claimant_was_represented_in_prior_suits) or prior_court_lacked_competent_jurisdiction)

predicates.suit_to_challenge_prior_execution_sale: A claimant brought a suit challenging an execution sale after earlier suits concerning the property had been decided.
predicates.claimant_was_party_to_prior_suits: The claimant was a party to the earlier suits concerning the property.
predicates.claimant_was_represented_in_prior_suits: The claimant was represented in the earlier suits by a person whose representation bound the claimant.
predicates.prior_court_lacked_competent_jurisdictio: The court that decided the earlier suits lacked competent jurisdiction for the matter at issue.

issues.definition: A challenge to an execution sale is not barred when the claimant was neither a party to nor represented in the earlier suits, or when the earlier suits were decided by a court lacking competent jurisdiction.
